quote: I looked into the whole thing before, but I didn't like it because of the prices, because of the terms, and a lot of stuff.
stewart_read: Customer discloses a specific prior solar experience with pricing/terms objections but the rep never asks which company or what the terms were.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged this as low-value since the call was heading toward a quick qualify-or-DQ path, making a deep probe unnecessary time investment.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to spend 10-15 seconds asking 'which company, what didn't you like about the terms' — this is free competitive intel even on calls that may DQ, since the follow-up note could carry that context forward.

quote: You have a very beautiful home, gets lots and lots of sunlight, so that's great to see.
stewart_read: Rep inserts a light personal compliment mid-verify to keep tone conversational rather than mechanical, which softens what is otherwise a rapid-fire qualifier sequence.
coaching_implication: This is a good habit to reinforce — brief, natural asides during Verify keep the call from feeling like an interrogation.

quote: And it looks like did you put, about a 100 to a 150 to how much you're currently paying?
stewart_read: Rep reads back a bill range apparently already on file (possibly a recycled/prior lead) rather than asking the customer directly, and gets only a flat confirmation.
coaching_implication: Even when a figure is pre-filled, the rep should get the customer to restate or react to it ('does $100-150 still sound right?') to create an anchor moment rather than a rubber-stamp confirmation.

stewart_read: The bill figure is confirmed and then immediately filed ('Write that down') with zero acknowledgment of what that spend means or any forward-pulling hook, even though the call ultimately DQ's minutes later.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic deferral is plausible if the rep intended to build the bill hook only after clearing the credit qualifier — but the credit question comes right after, so there was no later moment to return to it.
coaching_implication: Even on calls likely to disqualify, a one-line acknowledgment of the bill pain keeps the customer warm for the promised follow-up in a couple of months.

quote: And then in order to qualify for the current programs going on right now, all we ask of the homeowner is you just have a credit score of at least 670.
stewart_read: Rep states the correct 670 threshold (matching schema, unlike the 650 drift seen in other calls) and asks it as a direct yes/no gate.
coaching_implication: No coaching correction needed here — the number matches policy and the question is asked cleanly for both title holders.

quote: Yeah. Well, unfortunately, then it wouldn't really make sense as of right now. I I'll make a note here to follow-up with you in a couple of months just to see where everything's kind of at, but I'll take you off our list for now.
stewart_read: The rep closes the DQ with a vague future promise ('a couple of months') rather than a dated callback or any concrete next step, and there is no 'is that fair?' handshake or confirmation of contact method.
alternative_hypothesis: Given this is a hard DQ (credit), a full button-up script may not be warranted since there is no appointment to protect — the looser language may be appropriate for a non-appointment close.
coaching_implication: Even on a DQ, a specific timeframe or method for the follow-up (e.g., 'I'll check back with you in March by text') gives the lead a concrete reason to stay receptive rather than a vague, easily-forgotten promise.
